reason: Schedule lens: as described, the path to a scored probe has three unscheduled prerequisites in series, so P(scored before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC) is about 0.15, well below 0.7. (1) MODEL CODE UNKNOWN. The only evidence about the dataset is a README summary: research/browser_research_2026-09-24_pass2.md l.76 (pool=2, sigma 0.8 um, base ch 24, 128/32 D1.json, recall@4um top-330 0.7348, 46 MB). github.com/georgexue666 returns 404, WebSearch finds no repo, kaggle.com is blocked here (curl 000). Whether the dataset holds inference code, input normalisation, z-pooling and peak extraction is exactly browser_todo item 7, still open. Guess: P(usable code, or rebuilt from state_dict keys in <= 4 h) ~0.55. The licence is also unverified: pass2 l.238 says CC0, but h_kaggle-intel's own browser_todo still asks 'license (CC0?)'. (2) THE LAB REPLAY DOES NOT EXIST. 'Replay on friend A's x138 lab cache' needs two things. First, a cache that nobody has built: CONTEXT.md 25 Sep 10:20 and PROMPT_FRIEND_A.md top block tell friend A to WAIT for #34 (score due ~17-20 UTC 25 Sep) before starting it; his PC rebooted on 24 Sep and he has made no commits since 24 Sep 04:12 MSK. Second, a replay tool for the x138 tail: experiments/l2_daughternet/replay/replay.py has 0 occurrences of readmit / flow_predictor / gapfill, so the flow relink, readmit and gap filler that variant (b) and the head's gain depend on would have to be ported first. Friend A's GPU is also already promised to the x138 lab cache for division-insertion tuning (199 videos, several hours on the 5070 Ti), so this idea competes with it for his machine. P(friend A available AND x138 cache AND replay port by ~27 Sep 12:00) ~0.3-0.4. (3) BUILD AND RUNTIME. tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 supports only divinsert/leafprune, so a new patch type is needed (2-4 h of agent work plus tests). The extra UNet pass on the hidden run is unmeasured. The per-movie GPU seconds for x138 are themselves an open browser_todo item (exp56 logs), and x138 already has a 27,000 s runtime guard that switches relink, readmit and gap-fill off for late movies (experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md l.97). The 'runtime-guard fix' the idea bundles in is a separate, unbuilt change. The chain multiplies to 0.9 (browser in time) x 0.55 (code) x 0.35 (friend A, cache and replay) x 0.85 (build and dummy run clean) x 0.9 (hidden run within guard and 12 h) = ~0.13-0.17. The idea's own '48 h to scored probe, earliest 27 Sep 11:00' assumes every step succeeds on the first try. The date arithmetic is right (submit 27 Sep ~01:00 + 7-10 h latency), but it ignores the missing cache and replay tool. Numbers checked: recall@4 0.7348, team easonyanyan 0.950 (pass2 l.76, l.114), V1284 +0.007 on x138 and +0.002 on ours (CONTEXT 25 Sep 07:50), swap FN oracle and the 8.65 um a_never median (BRIEF, r1_hyp_detection). All match their sources. Validity caveat that affects the gate: 44b6 clips are overlapping crops of ONE recording (BRIEF), so the D1-val 44b6 movies are NOT out-of-sample for the precision model and the per-embryo gate is biased in its favour on 44b6. D1 = 128 + 32 = 160 of 199 movies; the missing 39 are unexplained.
fix_if_any: A Kaggle-only path, variant (a) only, with hard kill points; it drops friend A and the x138 replay from the critical path. K0: browser item 7 must deliver the file list, licence, code or state_dict key dump, and D1.json by 26 Sep 06:00 UTC, else drop the idea. G1 (gate kernel, Kaggle): attach the dataset, the competition train data and the existing capture outputs vitaliineibauer/biohub-chcap-* (V1284 inputs and integer peaks for all 199 videos, CONTEXT 24 Sep 23:00). Run the precision model on the 6bba D1-val movies only; report 44b6 separately and treat it as NOT out-of-sample. Apply the public V1284 head to the captures and compute GT distance, the within-4 um share and 7 um match counts for the fused positions (r 1.5/2.0 um, w 0.3/0.5/0.7). Run it on a free CPU kernel tonight with ~10 frames per movie (~2 h), or on GPU right after the 26 Sep 00:00 reset (~1-1.5 GPU-h). Gate as pre-registered, but the both-embryos requirement becomes 6bba out-of-sample plus 44b6 not worse. Drop variant (b) (readmit): it cannot be validated without an x138-tail replay, and it adds nodes (node-multiplier risk). B1: new build_probe_kernel patch 'precloc' on --base x138 (2-4 h). The fused positions replace the refined arr after the V1284 refine; with ENABLE=0 the output is byte-identical to exp56. Log per-movie extra GPU seconds. B2: a dummy run on the 4 visible movies; compare the per-movie time with the exp56 log. Kill if the extra time is > 10% of x138's per-movie time, unless the runtime-guard change has been built and tested separately. Only then is the slot spent. Repaired timeline: gate result 26 Sep ~08:00, build 08:00-12:00, dummy run 12:00-13:00, submit ~13:30 with the user's OK, scored 26 Sep ~21:00-23:30 UTC. That leaves ~2.5 days of slack for one retry. Even repaired, P(scored probe by 29 Sep 10:00 | gate passes) ~0.35 (0.9 x 0.55 x 0.85 x 0.85 x 0.95), and unconditionally ~0.1 because the gate itself passes with ~0.3 (guess). The code-availability unknown alone keeps it below 0.7. It would clear 0.7 only if item 7 shows ready-to-run inference code in the dataset.
realistic_public_gain: E ~ +0.0005 (range -0.002..+0.004). This is the idea's own E +0.001 (0.2 x ~+0.004) multiplied by P(a scored probe exists) ~0.35-0.5 on the repaired path. Variant (b) gives nothing, because it cannot be honestly validated in time.
realistic_private_gain: E ~ +0.0005 or less. The same localisation effect applies, but the extra GPU pass raises the chance that late hidden movies hit x138's 27,000 s guard (relink, readmit and gap-fill off), which would cost more on the larger private share. The 44b6 half of the gate is not out-of-sample, so embryo transfer is less certain than claimed.
